name: Average spine
about: A typical adult spine with no sideways curve, stacked from general measurements. Start here and shape it into your own.

name: One curve in the chest
about: A single curve of 45° to the right from T5 to T12, with the bodies turned. The most common pattern in teenagers with scoliosis.

name: A strong curve in the chest
about: The same pattern at 70°, with more turn in the bodies.

name: Two curves in the chest
about: A short curve of 30° to the left high in the chest and a larger one of 50° to the right below it.

name: Two curves, an S shape
about: A curve of 50° to the right in the chest and one of 40° to the left in the lower back.

name: Three curves
about: A curve high in the chest to the left, a larger one in the chest to the right and a third in the lower back to the left.

name: One curve in the lower back
about: A single curve of 35° to the left from T11 to L4.

name: A large curve low down, a smaller one above
about: A curve of 55° to the left where the chest meets the lower back and a smaller one of 38° to the right above it.

name: One long curve, a C shape
about: A single long curve of 60° to the left that runs from the upper chest to the lower back.

name: Round upper back
about: The chest part rounds backward by about 65°, where 20° to 40° is usual. Seen from the side. This is the shape that goes with Scheuermann's kyphosis.

name: Flat lower back
about: The lower back has lost most of its hollow, so the trunk leans forward. Seen from the side.

name: Deep hollow in the lower back
about: The lower back hollows by about 60°, more than usual. Seen from the side.

name: Fusion with screws at every level
about: A curve in the chest after surgery: fused from T4 to L1 with a screw on each side of every vertebra, two rods and a cross-link. Made up, not a real person.

name: Fusion with hooks on top and screws below
about: What is left of an S shape after surgery: fused from T4 to L4, with hooks on the top two levels, screws below, two rods and two cross-links. Made up, not a real person.

name: One rod with a hook at each end
about: The way many fusions were done from the 1960s into the 1990s: one straight rod on the inner side of the curve, held by a hook at each end. Fused from T4 to L2. Made up, not a real person.

name: A real spine: scoliosis fusion, T4 to L2, rods to L4
about: Made from the CT, MRI and X-rays of the person who started this project, shared by him as an example. Positions are his real ones. The bone shapes are drawn by the app.
